idiom_name: goroutine-per-connection over the runtime netpoller (channels and select for other event sources)
implementation_notes: The runtime's integrated network poller is the Reactor inside the language runtime: netpollinit/netpollopen arm edge-triggered notifications for a descriptor (epoll, kqueue, event ports, IOCP), netpoll returns the goroutines that netpollready marked ready, and the scheduler resumes exactly those goroutines. The application never sees a handle set or a dispatch table: what replaces the classic structure is blocking-style code inside a goroutine per connection (or a bounded worker set) plus select over channels when several event sources must be multiplexed. The classic form is justified only at the edge - syscall.RawConn or a foreign event loop - and there the code must drive its own poller and re-enter the runtime deliberately.
pitfalls: Descriptors obtained through os.NewFile or raw syscalls are not registered with the netpoller unless they are put in non-blocking mode explicitly, so a read on them blocks an OS thread and steals it from the scheduler.
cgo calls and long syscall.RawConn loops block the OS thread and bypass the poller; a reactor built around them must re-enter the runtime deliberately.

Unbounded accepts spawn unbounded goroutines - the loop has no admission control, so a semaphore or worker pool is the back-pressure surface, and a connection goroutine that fails before its defer leaks its slot.
